doc.title: Tim Ries interviewed by Monk Rowe, Utica, New York, March 19, 2022

title: The Universal Spirits Ensemble
summary: Ries describes his multinational group aiming at goodwill, which played the Carter Center.

story.theme_name: Race and segregation in the jazz life
story.community_name: Politics, race and the state of the country

blocks.x: sounding thing and I’m playing a wooden mouthpiece so I try to have the like low resonance of — so I don’t know, I mean I do my best to humanize it and, you know, in all of this thing I should just maybe end with saying about this ensemble that I have called the Universal Spirits Ensemble and it’s a group of musicians — it was originally for the idea of the conflict that was happening with the Israeli-Palestinian-Lebanese because I figured okay this is thirty years ago but now the world is just everything is crazy everywhere including in this country. So the band is like Israeli, Palestinian, Lebanese, Afghani, South African, Cuban, Puerto Rican, so it’s like a really mixed group of people, not really talking about religion or politics but just like these — the world is playing together. So the idea is to go around the world into smaller communities where maybe somebody lives two hours away from a big city but maybe they won’t go to that city, I want to take the city to them, take the world to them teaching young kids to see them maybe like in a community with like a high school kid and maybe have this young flute player playing with a South African and an Afghani and a Palestinian musician and maybe that changes her life forever and maybe that changes that community to like last night in this small community, you know, how do you connect with that community. So we’re creating ambassadors for peace and goodwill across the world. So we’re playing in New York April 6th at the great place called Drom, D–R-O-M — and President Carter invited us to play at the Carter Center so we played there. So hopefully that group can do more as it comes — that’s what I’m focusing on is that ambassadorship of goodwill through this music.
